hints: Identify the given marginal totals: total adults = 30, right-handed total = 25, and spectacles total = 8.
Fill in the given cell: 19 adults are right-handed and do not wear spectacles. Subtract 19 from the right-handed total of 25 to find how many right-handed adults wear spectacles.
Use row and column subtractions to find the remaining entries: total not wearing spectacles is $30 - 8 = 22$, and total not right-handed is $30 - 25 = 5$.
walkthrough:
Start by identifying the given counts and totals for the group of 30 adults:
$$\text{Overall total} = 30$$
$$\text{Right-handed total} = 25 \implies \text{Not right-handed total} = 30 - 25 = 5$$
$$\text{Spectacles total} = 8 \implies \text{No spectacles total} = 30 - 8 = 22$$

Next, insert the given intersection count into the right-handed row:
$$\text{Right-handed without spectacles} = 19$$
Because the right-handed row must sum to 25, find the number of right-handed adults who wear spectacles:
$$25 - 19 = 6$$

Now complete the 'Not right-handed' row using column totals:
For the 'Wears spectacles' column (which totals 8):
$$\text{Not right-handed with spectacles} = 8 - 6 = 2$$
For the 'Does not wear spectacles' column (which totals 22):
$$\text{Not right-handed without spectacles} = 22 - 19 = 3$$

Check consistency along the 'Not right-handed' row:
$$2 + 3 = 5$$
The row total matches 5, confirming all entries are correct:
$$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|}
\hline
& \text{Spectacles} & \text{No spectacles} & \text{Total} \\
\hline
\text{Right-handed} & 6 & 19 & 25 \\
\hline
\text{Not right-handed} & 2 & 3 & 5 \\
\hline
\text{Total} & 8 & 22 & 30 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

hints: State the mathematical condition for events $X$ and $Y$ to be independent: $\mathrm{P}(X \cap Y) = \mathrm{P}(X) \times \mathrm{P}(Y)$ (or $\mathrm{P}(X \mid Y) = \mathrm{P}(X)$).
Read the relevant probabilities from your table: $\mathrm{P}(X) = \dfrac{25}{30}$, $\mathrm{P}(Y) = \dfrac{8}{30}$, and $\mathrm{P}(X \cap Y) = \dfrac{6}{30}$.
Compute the product $\mathrm{P}(X) \times \mathrm{P}(Y)$ and compare it directly to $\mathrm{P}(X \cap Y)$ to draw your conclusion.
walkthrough:
To determine whether two events $X$ and $Y$ are independent, we must test whether the probability of both occurring equals the product of their separate probabilities:
$$\text{Condition for independence: } \mathrm{P}(X \cap Y) = \mathrm{P}(X) \times \mathrm{P}(Y)$$

From the completed two-way table, find the probabilities:
$$\mathrm{P}(X) = \mathrm{P}(\text{right-handed}) = \frac{25}{30} = \frac{5}{6}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(Y) = \mathrm{P}(\text{wears spectacles}) = \frac{8}{30} = \frac{4}{15}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X \cap Y) = \mathrm{P}(\text{right-handed and wears spectacles}) = \frac{6}{30} = \frac{1}{5}$$

Compare the two numerical fractions by writing them with a common denominator of 45:
$$\mathrm{P}(X \cap Y) = \frac{1}{5} = \frac{9}{45}$$
$$\mathrm{P}(X) \times \mathrm{P}(Y) = \frac{2}{9} = \frac{10}{45}$$
Since $\frac{9}{45} \ne \frac{10}{45}$, we have $\mathrm{P}(X \cap Y) \ne \mathrm{P}(X) \times \mathrm{P}(Y)$.
Therefore, events $X$ and $Y$ are not independent.
